source_input: Client use case 1, 'Certificate Update Automation': "Certificate update by automation for all kinds of load balancer devices: F5, NetScaler, Radware, Anaya LB." The client's stated aim for all use cases is "to do automation using Claude for all these content" with titles on the line of "Automation of <> using Claude".
why_this_course: Expired certificates are one of the most avoidable causes of outages on load balancers, and renewal is about to become much more frequent. The CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements cut the maximum validity of publicly trusted TLS certificates from 398 days to 200 days in March 2026, 100 days in March 2027 and 47 days in March 2029 [c18]. A team that renews a few hundred certificates by hand once a year will soon be doing it several times a year on every load balancer they own.

The hard part is not getting a certificate; ACME already automates issuance [c5]. The hard part is putting it on the right objects on each platform: F5 certificate and key files referenced from client-ssl profiles [c1][c10], NetScaler cert-key pairs bound to every SSL virtual server [c3], Alteon certificates applied through a separate step [c4], and HA pairs that must be synchronized [c13]. Each platform has its own API and its own failure modes.

This course teaches teams to use Claude where it helps most (reading inventory, drafting plans and code, explaining) while keeping every device write in deterministic, tested code behind a human approval. That split follows OWASP guidance on limiting agent permissions and requiring human approval for high-impact actions [c28], and it gives the client a pipeline they can audit.

design_decisions.decision: Cover F5, NetScaler and Radware in depth and Anaya LB through an adapter
design_decisions.rationale: The client named all four. F5, NetScaler and Radware have public API documentation [c1][c2][c29]; we could not find public documentation for Anaya LB, so the course builds a shared adapter contract that the client can implement against their own Anaya documentation.

design_decisions.decision: Claude plans and drafts; deterministic code executes
design_decisions.rationale: Certificate installs touch production traffic. Keeping writes in tested Python, with the model limited to read-only tools, follows OWASP's excessive-agency mitigations [c28] and makes behavior repeatable.

design_decisions.decision: Start with a manual renewal before any automation
design_decisions.rationale: Learners need to see where outages come from (chain, key match, missed binding, HA sync) before they can write checks that catch them.

design_decisions.decision: ServiceNow change records and approval as the gate
design_decisions.rationale: The client's other use cases already center on ServiceNow (SNOW). Using the Table API [c24] and Flow Designer approval [c25] fits existing change practice.

design_decisions.decision: Keys and CSRs generated by code, never by the model
design_decisions.rationale: Private keys must never enter prompts or logs. Generating CSRs in code with a standard library [c27] keeps key material out of the model's context.

design_decisions.decision: GitHub pull requests and Actions for review and CI
design_decisions.rationale: Reviewing renewal plans like code gives a second human view and a test record; scheduling through Actions [c26] gives a simple way to run inventory daily.

audience_profile.needs: A safe, repeatable way to renew certificates across platforms

audience_profile.needs: Visibility of where each certificate is bound and proof of renewal
audience_profile.starting_point: Strong on certificates and CAs; limited load balancer knowledge

audience_profile.needs: A pattern for using an AI assistant safely in production change
audience_profile.starting_point: Comfortable with Python, Git and REST APIs

audience_profile.role: Enterprise IT and network operations staff
audience_profile.needs: To run and support the pipeline day to day
audience_profile.starting_point: Familiar with change management and ServiceNow

prerequisite_check: Can you find which virtual servers use a given certificate on at least one platform you manage?
Can you explain the difference between a leaf certificate, an intermediate and a root?
Can you read and run a short Python script and make a commit in Git?
Can you call a REST API with curl and read a JSON response?
Do you have, or can you get, a laptop that can reach the lab over SSH and HTTPS?

lab_environment.overview: Each learner gets a small estate: an F5 BIG-IP VE pair, a NetScaler VPX, an Alteon VA, a step-ca ACME lab CA, a ServiceNow developer instance and a GitHub repository. All certificates are issued by the lab CA for example.corp names. Recorded API responses let every test run offline.

components.how_to_obtain: Client to provide API documentation or a test device
components.notes: No public documentation was found; the course ships a stub.

safety: Lab devices only; no production addresses in any config file
All certificates come from the lab CA for example.corp names
Device credentials only in environment variables or the lab vault, never in prompts or the repository
The MCP server exposes read-only tools; device writes only through executors with an approved change
Reset scripts restore every device to its baseline at the end of each day

modules.title: Certificate lifecycle on load balancers and the automation baseline
modules.goal: Learners understand exactly where a certificate lives and is bound on each platform, and where manual renewals fail, before any automation is written.
learning_objectives: Learners can trace a certificate from file object to virtual server on F5, NetScaler and Alteon
Learners can name the four most common renewal outage causes and show where each happens
Learners can explain why shorter certificate lifetimes make manual renewal unsustainable
Learners can state the course operating pattern: Claude plans, code executes, a human approves, everything is logged

lessons.title: F5 BIG-IP: files, profiles, virtual servers
points: Certificates and keys are separate file objects: /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert and /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-key, each keyed by name, partition and subPath [c1][c14]
A client-ssl profile references the pair through certKeyChain; the older cert and chain properties are deprecated [c10]
A client-ssl profile needs at least one cert/key pair; tmsh edits it with cert-key-chain add, modify or replace-all-with [c11]
The profile, not the certificate, is attached to the virtual server, so one certificate can sit behind many virtual servers through shared profiles
Every ssl-cert object exposes expirationDate, subject, issuer, subjectAlternativeName and serialNumber, which is what inventory will read [c1]

lessons.title: NetScaler: cert-key pairs and vserver bindings
points: Files sit in /nsconfig/ssl by default; add ssl certKey creates a named pair that points at the files [c3]
Intermediates must be linked to the server cert-key pair before binding (linkcertkeyname in NITRO) [c3][c2]
Each SSL virtual server needs its own binding: bind ssl vserver <vs> -certkeyName <name>, checked with show ssl vserver [c3]
Built-in expiry monitoring exists (expirymonitor, notificationperiod 10 to 100 days) but only alerts; it never renews [c2]
Updating a pair in place (update ssl certKey, NITRO ?action=update) swaps the files under every existing binding at once [c2]

lessons.title: Radware Alteon and other platforms (Anaya LB)
points: Alteon CLI installation: one PEM with server cert then intermediates, entered under cfg then cert, terminated with three periods, then apply [c4]
Configuration changes are pending until applied; treat apply and save as explicit, separate steps in every runbook
Radware publishes a Python SDK over the Alteon REST backend with an SSL key configurator, which the course uses as the API reference point [c29]
Anaya LB has no public API documentation we could verify; the course treats it through an adapter that the client fills in against their own device documentation

lessons.title: Where renewal outages really come from
points: Wrong or missing chain: the leaf is valid but clients cannot build a path; openssl s_client -showcerts shows what the server really sends [c20]
Key and certificate mismatch: the object installs but the handshake fails
Binding missed on one of several virtual servers or SNI profiles, especially where sniDefault decides the fallback profile [c10]
HA pair not synchronized after the change, so the standby still serves the old certificate after failover [c13]
Public certificate lifetimes drop to 200 days from March 2026, 100 days from March 2027 and 47 days from March 2029, so renewals become frequent routine work [c18]

lessons.title: The operating pattern and the lab estate
points: Claude reads, plans, drafts code and explains; deterministic Python performs every device write
Every write needs an approved change and a named human approver; the agent cannot self-approve [c28]
Lab estate: lb-f5-01 (with a standby peer), lb-ns-01, lb-rw-01, a step-ca ACME lab CA and a ServiceNow developer instance [c31][c33]
Everything is logged: prompts, tool calls, device requests and responses, approver and time

instructor_demo: Open the F5 GUI and REST side by side; GET /mgmt/tm/ltm/profile/client-ssl/~Common~clientssl_payments and point to certKeyChain
GET the referenced ssl-cert object and read expirationString, serialNumber and subjectAlternativeName aloud
On lb-ns-01 run show ssl certKey and show ssl vserver vs_portal_443 to show the binding and linked intermediate
Run openssl s_client -connect portal.example.corp:443 -servername portal.example.corp -showcerts against both devices and compare chains
Renew one F5 certificate by hand and deliberately skip config sync; fail over and show the old serial being served
Draw the failure-point map on the whiteboard as learners call out each step

lab.brief: Renew one certificate by hand on lb-f5-01 and one on lb-ns-01 using a lab CA certificate, writing down every step and every point where a mistake would cause an outage.
steps: Request a certificate for pay.example.corp from the step-ca lab CA using the CSR provided
On F5, import the key and certificate with date-suffixed names through the GUI or tmsh
Update clientssl_payments cert-key-chain to the new pair and confirm with tmsh list ltm profile client-ssl clientssl_payments
Run tmsh run cm config-sync to-group <device group> and confirm the peer shows in sync
On NetScaler, copy files to /nsconfig/ssl, add the cert-key pair, link the intermediate and bind it to vs_portal_443
Verify both with openssl s_client -showcerts and record the new serial numbers
Write each step into the runbook template with the time it took
Mark every step on the failure-point map with what would go wrong and how you would detect it
success_criteria: Both virtual servers serve the new serial with a complete chain
The F5 standby holds the same certificate objects after sync
The runbook lists every step, command and verification
The failure-point map covers chain, key match, missed binding and HA sync at minimum

common_pitfalls: Overwriting the existing certificate object instead of creating a new date-suffixed object, which removes the rollback path
Forgetting to link the intermediate on NetScaler before binding
Checking only the active F5 unit and not the standby
Trusting the browser view of the chain, which may fill gaps from its own cache, instead of s_client -showcerts

knowledge_check.q: On F5, what attaches a certificate to a virtual server?
knowledge_check.a: A client-ssl profile whose certKeyChain references the cert and key objects; the profile is then attached to the virtual server.

knowledge_check.q: Why does NetScaler expiry monitoring not solve the renewal problem?
knowledge_check.a: expirymonitor and notificationperiod only raise an alert before expiry; they do not request, install or bind a new certificate.

knowledge_check.q: What does openssl s_client -showcerts show that a browser may not?
knowledge_check.a: Only the certificates the server actually sent, in order, without filling in missing intermediates.

knowledge_check.q: Why will renewal frequency increase over the next few years?
knowledge_check.a: The CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements cut maximum public certificate validity to 200 days in 2026, 100 days in 2027 and 47 days in 2029.

modules.title: Setting up Claude Code, the Agent SDK and MCP for certificate work
modules.goal: Learners build a workbench where Claude can read certificate data through narrow read-only tools and cannot change any device.
learning_objectives: Learners can install Claude Code and write a project CLAUDE.md that encodes estate conventions and red lines
Learners can define typed tools with the Agent SDK and expose them through an MCP server
Learners can block unwanted tool calls with permissions and PreToolUse hooks
Learners can keep device credentials out of prompts, logs and the repository

lessons.title: Claude Code and the project file
points: Install with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash on macOS, Linux or WSL; claude -p runs it non-interactively for scripts and CI [c8]
Project instructions live in ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md and are shared through source control [c30]
Put naming rules in CLAUDE.md: <fqdn>_<YYYYMMDD> for certificate objects, clientssl_<app> for profiles
State red lines plainly: never call write endpoints, never read files under secrets/, never print key material
Keep CLAUDE.md short and specific; long files cost context and reduce adherence [c30]

lessons.title: Agent SDK tools with schemas
points: Define each tool with @tool (name, description, input schema, handler), wrap them with create_sdk_mcp_server and pass them in mcp_servers [c22]
Tool names become mcp__certops__list_certs and must be listed in allowed_tools to run without a prompt [c22]
Mark read tools with readOnlyHint and return machine-readable results in structuredContent alongside text [c22]
Return isError: true with a clear message when a device call fails so the model does not invent data [c22]
The SDK uses API-key authentication for anything you ship to others [c9]

lessons.title: A read-only certificate MCP server
points: Three tools only: list_certs(device), get_expiry(device, cert), get_bindings(device, cert)
No write tool exists in the server, so a prompt cannot reach a write path
MCP standardizes how tools are described and called, so the same server works from Claude Code and the Agent SDK [c7]
Each tool returns typed records validated before they are returned

lessons.title: Guardrails at the workbench
points: PreToolUse hooks run before a tool call and can deny it with a reason; use one to block any Bash call containing curl -X POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE against device addresses [c21]
Credentials come from environment variables injected from a vault at process start, never from prompts
Redact Authorization, Cookie and X-NITRO-PASS headers in every log line [c2]
Least privilege on devices too: the read tools use a read-only device account [c28]

instructor_demo: Create the repo, run claude in it and write CLAUDE.md live with the naming rules and red lines
Write list_certs for F5 with @tool, returning name, expirationDate and serialNumber from /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert
Register the server and show the tool name mcp__certops__list_certs in the session
Ask Claude to explain bindings on lb-f5-01 and show it calling only read tools
Ask Claude to replace the certificate and show the request refused because no write tool exists and the hook denies device writes
Show the log file with secrets redacted

lab.brief: Build the read-only certificate MCP server, connect it to Claude Code and ask Claude to explain the bindings on lb-f5-01 without changing anything.
steps: Clone the starter repo and create a Python virtual environment
Write CLAUDE.md with naming conventions, lab hostnames and red lines
Implement list_certs, get_expiry and get_bindings for F5 against the recorded responses in fixtures/f5/
Add readOnlyHint to every tool and return structuredContent
Register the server in Claude Code and confirm the three tools appear
Add a PreToolUse hook that denies any shell command sending POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to a device address
Point the tools at lb-f5-01 using credentials from environment variables
Ask Claude which virtual servers depend on pay.example.corp and save the answer
success_criteria: Claude answers using only tool results and names the profile and virtual servers correctly
A request to change the certificate is refused and the refusal is logged
No credential appears in the repo, the transcript or the log
pytest passes for all three tools against recorded responses

common_pitfalls: Exposing a generic run_command tool, which turns a read-only server into a write path
Putting the device password in CLAUDE.md or a prompt 'just for the lab'
Returning free text from tools so the model has to guess at field meanings
Relying on tool annotations alone; MCP treats them as hints, so enforcement must be in code and hooks

knowledge_check.q: What makes a tool callable without a prompt in the Agent SDK?
knowledge_check.a: Listing its full name, mcp__{server}__{tool}, in allowed_tools.

knowledge_check.q: Where should the rule 'never call write endpoints' be enforced?
knowledge_check.a: In code: no write tools in the server plus a PreToolUse hook; CLAUDE.md states the rule but is not enforcement.

knowledge_check.q: What should a tool return when the device call fails?
knowledge_check.a: isError: true with a clear message, so Claude reports the failure instead of inventing data.

modules.title: Certificate inventory and expiry discovery across platforms
modules.goal: Learners build collectors that turn three different APIs into one typed inventory, with unknowns marked rather than guessed.
learning_objectives: Learners can read certificates, profiles and bindings from F5 iControl REST and NetScaler NITRO
Learners can map Alteon certificate data through the Radware SDK or REST backend behind an adapter
Learners can define a typed inventory record with a confidence field
Learners can review Claude-drafted collector code and test it against recorded responses

lessons.title: F5 collection
points: GET /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert returns every certificate with expirationDate, subjectAlternativeName, issuer and serialNumber [c1]
GET /mgmt/tm/ltm/profile/client-ssl returns certKeyChain entries that map profiles to cert and key names [c10]
Map profiles to virtual servers by reading each virtual server's profiles list; verify a sample with tmsh list ltm profile client-ssl [c11]
Collect partitions explicitly; objects outside /Common are easy to miss

lessons.title: NetScaler collection
points: Log in with POST /nitro/v1/config/login and send Cookie: NITRO_AUTH_TOKEN on later calls [c2]
GET /nitro/v1/config/sslcertkey returns pairs with daystoexpiration and linked CA pair names [c2]
GET /nitro/v1/config/sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding/<vservername> returns the certkeyname and whether it is an SNI or CA binding [c15]
Use ?count=yes to check totals before paging through large estates [c2]

lessons.title: Alteon and the adapter interface
points: The Radware alteon-sdk reads SSL keys and certificates through configurators over the REST backend; it requires Alteon 31.0.10.0 or 32.2.2.0 at minimum [c29]
Wrap every platform behind one interface: list_certificates(), list_bindings(), device_facts()
The Anaya LB adapter is a stub that returns UNKNOWN for every field until the client supplies its API details
Adapters normalize dates to UTC and serials to uppercase hex so rows compare across platforms

lessons.title: The typed inventory record
points: Fields: device, platform, cert_name, subject, sans, issuer, serial, not_after, chain_complete, bound_to, owner, confidence
confidence is high when the binding was read from the device, low when inferred, unknown when the source is missing
Owner comes from CMDB; a missing owner is recorded as UNKNOWN, never filled in by the model
Every row carries an ID such as inventory#f5-0031 so later plans can cite it

lessons.title: Claude drafts, you review
points: Ask Claude to draft each collector from the API reference and a recorded response
Review the diff line by line; reject any write call or unbounded retry
Test with pytest against recorded JSON; monkeypatch the HTTP client so tests never touch a device
Ask Claude to explain each field mapping and compare the explanation to the API reference

instructor_demo: Show raw JSON from F5 ssl-cert, client-ssl and a virtual server, and the joins needed between them
Show raw NITRO sslcertkey and sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding responses for lb-ns-01
Prompt Claude to draft the NetScaler collector and review the diff aloud, rejecting one unsafe change
Run pytest against recorded responses and show a failing test caught by a missing field
Generate the expiry report and point out rows marked UNKNOWN

lab.brief: Build the multi-platform inventory collector and produce one expiry report for the lab estate with unknowns marked explicitly.
steps: Define the inventory record as a dataclass or Pydantic model with the fields above
Ask Claude to draft the F5 collector; review and commit it
Ask Claude to draft the NetScaler collector including login and bindings; review and commit it
Implement the Alteon adapter against recorded responses
Add the Anaya LB stub that returns UNKNOWN
Write pytest cases for each collector with recorded responses
Join owner data from the ServiceNow CMDB export fixture
Produce expiry_report.csv and expiry_report.md sorted by not_after
success_criteria: Every certificate on the three lab devices appears once with its bindings
Rows with a missing owner or unverified binding are marked UNKNOWN or low confidence
All collector tests pass without network access
The report shows pay.example.corp bound to vs_payments_443 on lb-f5-01

common_pitfalls: Assuming certificate name equals hostname; match on SANs instead
Missing SNI bindings or non-Common partitions
Letting the model fill in a missing owner from the hostname
Tests that call a live device and pass only when the lab is up

knowledge_check.q: Which NITRO resource tells you which virtual servers use a cert-key pair?
knowledge_check.a: sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding, read per virtual server.

knowledge_check.q: Why does each inventory row carry an ID?
knowledge_check.a: So the planning agent can cite exact rows as evidence and reviewers can check them.

knowledge_check.q: What should the collector do when it cannot read a binding?
knowledge_check.a: Record the field as unknown with low confidence; never infer it silently.

modules.title: Renewal planning agent and ServiceNow change records
modules.goal: Learners build an agent that turns inventory into a cited JSON renewal plan and a ServiceNow change, with code, not the model, handling keys and CSRs.
learning_objectives: Learners can force the planning agent to return a plan that matches a JSON schema
Learners can make unknowns block a plan rather than be guessed
Learners can create and update change_request records through the Table API and route them to approval
Learners can generate keys and CSRs in code and obtain certificates from an ACME lab CA

lessons.title: Plan schema and structured output
points: Define the plan schema: steps[], each with device, cert, target_objects, window, blast_radius, evidence[] and rollback
Send the schema in output_config.format so the response matches it; use strict tool use for tool inputs [c23]
Validate the plan again in code before anything else reads it
Order by expiry first, then blast radius (number of virtual servers and business service)

lessons.title: Citations and blocking unknowns
points: Every step must cite inventory row IDs; the validator rejects steps without evidence
Any cited row with owner UNKNOWN or binding confidence low turns the plan status to BLOCKED with a reason
The agent may explain why a plan is blocked; it may not change the inventory to unblock it
A blocked plan is still saved and shown, so the owner gap becomes a visible task rather than a silent skip

lessons.title: ServiceNow change records
points: Create with POST /api/now/table/change_request (one record per call, 201 on success) [c24]
Update with PATCH /api/now/table/change_request/{sys_id}; read state with GET and sysparm_fields to keep payloads small [c24]
Put the plan summary, evidence row IDs and rollback command in the description and work notes
Use a Flow Designer flow with Ask for Approval on the change record; read the resulting approval state rather than assuming it [c25]
Give the approval a due date so a forgotten request resolves instead of waiting forever [c25]

lessons.title: Keys, CSRs and the ACME lab CA
points: Generate the key and CSR in the executor with x509.CertificateSigningRequestBuilder; the CA gets the CSR, never the key [c27]
ACME flow: order, prove control with a challenge, finalize with the CSR, download the certificate [c5]
In the lab, step-ca acts as the ACME CA after step ca provisioner add acme --type ACME [c31]
For internal CAs without ACME, the executor submits the CSR to the CA's request API and stores the returned chain
The model never sees key material; it only sees the CSR subject, SANs and the returned certificate serial

instructor_demo: Show the plan JSON schema and run the agent on the inventory fixture
Show a plan step citing inventory#f5-0031 and cmdb#9921
Remove the owner from one row and rerun to show the plan BLOCKED with a reason
Create the change through the Table API and show it in the ServiceNow developer instance
Trigger the approval flow and show the approval state read back by code
Run the ACME request from code and show the key file permissions and the absence of key data in the transcript

lab.brief: Run the planning agent on the inventory, inspect the JSON plan, and watch it open a change record that cites the exact certificates it will touch.
steps: Write the plan JSON schema and a validator
Implement the planning agent with the inventory tools and structured output
Run it on the lab inventory and save plan.json
Add the rule that UNKNOWN owner or low-confidence binding blocks the step, and test it
Implement create_change and update_change against the Table API
Build or import the Flow Designer approval flow for the lab change model
Implement request_certificate with key and CSR generation in code and ACME issuance from step-ca
Attach the plan JSON to the change record
success_criteria: plan.json validates against the schema and every step cites inventory rows
A row with a missing owner blocks its step with a logged reason
The change record exists with plan summary, evidence and rollback text
The issued certificate matches the CSR and no key material appears in any log or transcript

common_pitfalls: Letting the model write the CSR or handle the key 'to save time'
Assuming the change is approved because the API call succeeded
Free-text plans that cannot be validated
Hard-coding change state numbers without checking the instance's change model

knowledge_check.q: How does the course guarantee the plan's shape?
knowledge_check.a: A JSON schema sent through structured outputs, then validated again in code.

knowledge_check.q: What should happen if a cited inventory row has no owner?
knowledge_check.a: The step is blocked with a reason; the agent does not guess the owner.

knowledge_check.q: Which ACME step uses the CSR?
knowledge_check.a: Finalizing the order, after the identifier challenges are satisfied.

modules.title: Deterministic executor: F5 BIG-IP with iControl REST and tmsh
modules.goal: Learners build and test an F5 executor that installs a new certificate as new objects, swaps the profile, syncs the HA pair and verifies, with no model in the write path.
learning_objectives: Learners can upload files to BIG-IP through the file-transfer worker with chunking
Learners can create ssl-key and ssl-cert objects and update a client-ssl profile's certKeyChain
Learners can make the executor idempotent and HA-aware
Learners can test the executor against recorded iControl responses

lessons.title: Uploading files
points: POST /mgmt/shared/file-transfer/uploads/<filename> writes to /var/config/rest/downloads/ [c12]
Send Content-Range: start-end/filesize; files over 1M must be sent in chunks [c12]
Upload the key and certificate as separate files and remove them from the downloads directory after import
Check the upload response for the final byte count before creating objects

lessons.title: Creating objects and swapping the profile
points: Create the key at /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-key and the certificate at /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert with sourcePath file:/var/config/rest/downloads/<file> [c14][c1]
Name objects <fqdn>_<YYYYMMDD> so the previous object stays for rollback

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for certificate changes

lessons.title: Policy checks before any write

Device on the allow list for this change; anything else is BLOCKED

lessons.title: The human approval gate
points: Use Ask for Approval on the change record; branch on Approved and treat every other state as no [c25]

lessons.title: Scope limits
points: Executors check every step against the approved plan hash and refuse anything else
Hooks block the model from calling executors directly from a chat session [c21]

lessons.title: Audit trail
points: Append-only JSON lines: prompt, tool calls, plan hash, approver, timestamps, device requests and responses

common_pitfalls: Checking approval once at plan time and not again at execution time

Logs that can be edited after the fact

knowledge_check.q: Which approval states should allow a write?
knowledge_check.a: Only Approved; all others block.

knowledge_check.q: Why re-check HA sync immediately before writing?
knowledge_check.a: State can change between planning and execution; a write to an out-of-sync pair risks serving the old certificate after failover.

knowledge_check.q: How does the design stop the agent from approving its own change?
knowledge_check.a: Its service account has no approval rights and approval is read from ServiceNow, not from the agent.

capstone_plan.brief: Teams build and demonstrate a repeatable pipeline that discovers expiring certificates across F5, NetScaler, Radware and the Anaya LB adapter, has Claude draft a cited renewal plan and ServiceNow change, installs through tested executors only after human approval, validates every binding, rolls back on failure and leaves a full audit trail.

promo_video_research.hook_basis: The midnight-expiry hook is a teaching scenario, not a reported incident. It is realistic because NetScaler's own expiry monitoring only alerts and does not renew [c2], bindings are per virtual server [c3], and certificate lifetimes are shrinking toward 47 days, which multiplies renewal events [c18].

citations.title: APIRef_tm_sys_file_ssl-cert
citations.key_fact: The /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert collection supports GET; individual resources support GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, are keyed by name, partition and subPath, take a sourcePath (the URI the file is copied from) and expose read-only X.509 details including expirationDate, expirationString, subject, issuer, subjectAlternativeName, serialNumber and fingerprint.

citations.title: sslcertkey | configuration (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: Add is POST /nitro/v1/config/sslcertkey with mandatory certkey and cert; update is PUT with certkey plus expirymonitor and notificationperiod (10 to 100 days); the change operation is POST /nitro/v1/config/sslcertkey?action=update and accepts nodomaincheck; daystoexpiration is a read-only property; linkcertkeyname links a CA cert-key pair. Sessions start at /nitro/v1/config/login and use Cookie: NITRO_AUTH_TOKEN, or per-request X-NITRO-USER and X-NITRO-PASS headers.

citations.title: Create a certificate signing request and use SSL certificates on a NetScaler appliance
citations.key_fact: Certificates and keys live in /nsconfig/ssl by default; add ssl certKey <name> -cert <file> -key <file> [-expiryMonitor ENABLED -notificationPeriod <days>] creates the pair; intermediate certificates must be linked before binding; every SSL virtual server needs its own valid binding, made with bind ssl vserver <vs> -certkeyName <name> and checked with show ssl vserver <vs>.

citations.title: SSL Certificate Installation: Radware Alteon
citations.key_fact: On Alteon the installation flow is to build one PEM file with the server certificate followed by the intermediate chain, enter cfg then cert on the CLI, paste the PEM, end the input with three periods and then run apply; the page does not describe a separate save step (no public Radware page with the same detail could be fetched).

citations.title: RFC 8555: Automatic Certificate Management Environment (ACME)
citations.key_fact: After registering an account an ACME client submits an order, proves control of each identifier through a challenge (for example http-01 or dns-01), finalizes the order by submitting a PKCS#10 CSR and then downloads the issued certificate.

citations.title: openssl-verify
citations.key_fact: openssl verify checks certificate chains; -CAfile supplies trusted anchors, while -untrusted (repeatable) supplies intermediate certificates used only for chain building.

citations.title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
citations.key_fact: MCP is an open standard, described as a USB-C port for AI applications, that gives AI applications a standard way to connect to external data sources, tools and workflows.

citations.title: Claude Code overview
citations.key_fact: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool for the terminal, IDE, desktop and browser; on macOS, Linux and WSL it installs with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash, and it can run non-interactively with claude -p for piping and CI use.

citations.title: Agent SDK overview
citations.key_fact: The Agent SDK is a Python or TypeScript library that runs the Claude Code engine with its built-in tools, permissions, sessions and hooks; products built on it must use API-key authentication rather than claude.ai logins unless previously approved.

citations.title: APIRef_tm_ltm_profile_client-ssl
citations.key_fact: Client SSL profiles live at /mgmt/tm/ltm/profile/client-ssl (resource methods GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, POST; key name, partition, subPath); the cert and chain properties are DEPRECATED in favor of certKeyChain, and sniDefault marks the profile used when the client sends no known server name.

citations.title: ltm profile client-ssl (tmsh reference)
citations.key_fact: In tmsh, cert-key-chain is changed with add, delete, modify or replace-all-with, each entry naming cert, chain, key, passphrase and usage; a client-ssl profile requires at least one cert/key pair to work.

citations.title: Demystifying iControl REST Part 5: Transferring Files
citations.key_fact: POST /mgmt/shared/file-transfer/uploads/ writes files to /var/config/rest/downloads/; transfers are chunked with a Content-Range: start-end/filesize header, and any file larger than 1M must be chunked because the worker enforces that limit.

citations.title: cm config-sync (tmsh reference)
citations.key_fact: run cm config-sync starts a configuration synchronization job and must be given one of to-group, from-group or recover-sync to set the direction (force-full-load-push is also available).

citations.title: APIRef_tm_sys_file_ssl-key
citations.key_fact: Private keys are managed at /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-key; resources support GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and POST and are keyed by name, partition and subPath.

citations.title: sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: Bindings are added with PUT /nitro/v1/config/sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding (vservername mandatory, plus certkeyname, ca, snicert and ocspcheck) and read with GET /nitro/v1/config/sslvserver_sslcertkey_binding/<vservername>.

citations.title: systemfile (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: POST /nitro/v1/config/systemfile uploads a file with filename (no path), filecontent in Base64 and filelocation; fileencoding defaults to BASE64.

citations.title: nsconfig (NITRO API)
citations.key_fact: The running configuration is saved with POST /nitro/v1/config/nsconfig?action=save.

citations.title: Baseline Requirements for TLS Server Certificates
citations.key_fact: Maximum validity for publicly trusted TLS subscriber certificates is 398 days before 2026-03-15, 200 days from 2026-03-15, 100 days from 2027-03-15 and 47 days from 2029-03-15.

citations.title: RFC 6960: X.509 Internet PKI Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP)
citations.key_fact: OCSP responses report a certificate status of good, revoked or unknown, with thisUpdate and nextUpdate times; good means no certificate with that serial number in its validity interval is known to be revoked.

citations.title: openssl-s_client
citations.key_fact: openssl s_client -connect host:port opens a TLS connection; -servername sets SNI, -showcerts prints the certificates the server actually sent (not a verified chain) and -status requests an OCSP stapled response.

citations.title: Hooks reference
citations.key_fact: PreToolUse hooks run after Claude creates tool parameters and before the call is processed, match built-in and MCP tool names, and can block the call (exit code 2) or return permissionDecision deny with a reason.

citations.title: Give Claude custom tools (Agent SDK)
citations.key_fact: Python tools are defined with @tool, wrapped with create_sdk_mcp_server and passed in mcp_servers; their full names are mcp__{server_name}__{tool_name} and are pre-approved through allowed_tools; tools can set readOnlyHint, return structuredContent and return isError: true on failure.

citations.title: Structured outputs
citations.key_fact: JSON outputs send a JSON schema in output_config.format (type json_schema) so the response matches the schema, and strict tool use (strict: true) guarantees schema validation of tool names and inputs.

citations.title: Table API
citations.key_fact: The Table API provides GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on /api/now/table/{tableName} (and /{sys_id}); POST inserts one record and returns 201; GET filters with sysparm_query encoded queries and trims fields with sysparm_fields.

citations.title: Ask for Approval action
citations.key_fact: Ask for Approval takes a record, table, approval and rejection rules and an optional due date, and outputs an approval state (Requested, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled, No Longer Required, Skipped) that later flow steps can branch on.

citations.title: Events that trigger workflows
citations.key_fact: schedule runs on the latest commit of the default branch in UTC (optional IANA timezone), no more often than every 5 minutes, and may be delayed or dropped at high load such as the top of the hour; workflow_dispatch accepts typed inputs and needs the workflow file on the default branch.

citations.title: X.509 Tutorial
citations.key_fact: x509.CertificateSigningRequestBuilder builds and signs a CSR in Python; the usual flow is to generate a key pair, sign a CSR with it and give the CA the CSR but never the private key.

citations.title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
citations.key_fact: Mitigations include minimizing extension functionality and permissions and requiring human-in-the-loop approval of high-impact actions, implemented in a downstream system or the extension itself.

citations.title: alteon-sdk (Python package metadata)
citations.key_fact: alteon-sdk wraps the Alteon REST backend with 46 configurators (including SSLKeyConfigurator), management functions such as config commit, and deploy options dry_run, write_on_change and get_diff; minimum supported Alteon versions are 31.0.10.0 and 32.2.2.0.

citations.title: How Claude remembers your project (CLAUDE.md)
citations.key_fact: A project CLAUDE.md lives at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, is shared through source control and should hold build and test commands, coding standards, naming conventions and common workflows.

citations.title: ACME Basics (step-ca)
citations.key_fact: step-ca enables ACME with step ca provisioner add acme --type ACME and supports http-01, dns-01 and tls-alpn-01 challenges; after challenges succeed the client submits a CSR and the CA issues the certificate.

citations.title: NetScaler licensing (VPX Express)
citations.key_fact: VPX Express needs no license file and offers 20 Mbps bandwidth, a maximum of 250 SSL sessions and 20 Mbps SSL throughput; from release 14.1 build 29.65 it includes all Premium-license features.

citations.title: Understanding PDIs
citations.key_fact: Personal Developer Instances are free for Developer Program members; an instance unused for ten days is reclaimed and reset, and idle instances hibernate until the owner signs in to the Developer Site.
